question: What is the primary purpose of maintaining a steady supply of injection safety commodities?

options.A: To comply with local hospital aesthetic guidelines
options.B: To speed up the drug administration process for staff
options.C: To prevent infection transmission during clinical procedures
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of hospital administration

explanation: Injection safety commodities are primarily utilized to protect patients and staff from bloodborne pathogens and accidental injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h1)

question: Why does a disruption in the supply chain of injection safety commodities increase infection risks in healthcare settings?

options.A: Manufacturer prices drop significantly during local stockouts
options.B: Patients refuse to take injections when supplies are running low
options.C: Clinicians may be forced to reuse single-use devices due to scarcity
options.D: Expired medications become more potent over prolonged periods

explanation: When basic injection equipment is unavailable, resource-constrained settings risk dangerous practices like device reuse. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h1)

question: Which characteristic uniquely defines an auto-disable syringe?

options.A: It features a retractable needle that hides inside the syringe barrel
options.B: It automatically locks or breaks after a single use to prevent reuse
options.C: It mixes powdered medication and liquid diluent without human help
options.D: It can be sterilized in an autoclave multiple times without damage

explanation: Auto-disable syringes have a built-in mechanism that renders them inoperable after the initial injection. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h2)

question: What is the primary clinical function of a safety box in an injection workflow?

options.A: Transporting bulk medical supplies safely from the central pharmacy
options.B: Storing sterile reconstitution syringes before they are unpacked for use
options.C: Measuring exact dosages of liquid medications before drawing them up
options.D: Providing puncture-resistant containment for used sharps at the bedside

explanation: Safety boxes or sharps containers are engineered to safely isolate used needles and prevent accidental needlestick injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h2)

question: What does the term lead time refer to in medical inventory management?

options.A: The period a nurse spends documenting a patient's medication chart
options.B: The time it takes for a syringe to expire on the hospital shelf
options.C: The duration between placing an order and receiving the items
options.D: The maximum length of time safety boxes can remain open safely

explanation: Lead time accounts for the administrative and transport delay between order initiation and delivery. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h3)

question: Why is maintaining a buffer stock essential for primary healthcare clinics?

options.A: It prevents staff from ordering more supplies than the budget allows
options.B: It reduces the total storage space required for bulky safety boxes
options.C: It protects against unexpected surges in demand or delivery delays
options.D: It guarantees that older stock items are used before newer arrivals

explanation: Buffer stocks act as a crucial safety net when transport disruptions or sudden disease outbreaks increase supply consumption. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h3)

question: What is the first operational step a nurse takes when initiating a supply requisition at the ward level?

options.A: Conducting a physical count of existing usable stock
options.B: Contacting the federal ministry of health for direct grants
options.C: Discarding all expired safety boxes into the incinerator
options.D: Submitting an emergency purchase order to private vendors

explanation: An accurate physical inventory count is always the starting point for determining true replenishment needs. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h4)

question: A clinic receives a delivery of auto-disable syringes from the central medical store. What action should the receiving nurse take first?

options.A: Distribute all the new syringes immediately to the pediatric immunization unit
options.B: Inspect the delivered boxes for damage and verify counts against the manifest
options.C: Store the cartons in the facility basement without opening the packaging
options.D: Sign the delivery receipt immediately without checking the contents inside

explanation: Goods must always be inspected upon arrival to catch discrepancies, damaged items, or short shipments before signing off. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h4)

question: Where is a bin card typically placed within a hospital or clinic storage facility?

options.A: Affixed to the exterior entrance door of the main pharmacy store
options.B: Locked inside the medical director's private filing cabinet
options.C: Hanging directly on the storage shelf next to the specific item
options.D: Stored permanently in the central hospital accounts department

explanation: Bin cards are kept right beside their corresponding stock items to ensure immediate, real-time recording of inventory movements. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h5)

question: What is the primary function of a Logistics Management Information System (LMIS) in health commodity management?

options.A: Calculating individual nurse salaries based on clinical hours worked
options.B: Designing secure physical storage warehouses for heavy medical gear
options.C: Collecting and sharing timely data on stock levels and consumption
options.D: Diagnosing infectious diseases in patients requiring routine injections

explanation: An LMIS aggregates inventory data across facilities to improve forecasting, ordering, and supply chain visibility. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h5)

question: What inventory rotation principle dictates that items with the nearest expiry dates are issued first?
explanation: FEFO ensures that stock closest to its expiry date is utilized before newer shipments, minimizing wastage. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h6)

question: Why should medical supply cartons never be placed directly on the floor of a storage room?

options.A: It slows down the physical counting process during monthly audits
options.B: Building codes prohibit any items from touching horizontal surfaces
options.C: Moisture from the floor can seep into cartons and compromise sterility
options.D: It makes the floor impossible to sweep during routine facility cleaning

explanation: Pallets and elevated shelves protect medical commodities from ground moisture and potential pest damage. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is an appropriate immediate action for a clinic facing an unexpected stockout of auto-disable syringes?

options.A: Instructing clinicians to wash and reuse standard disposable syringes
options.B: Arranging an emergency inter-facility transfer from a nearby partner clinic
options.C: Suspending all patient immunization and injection services indefinitely
options.D: Administering oral medications instead of injections for all diagnoses

explanation: Emergency borrowing or transferring from nearby facilities helps bridge critical gaps safely without resorting to dangerous reuse practices. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of injection safety commodity wastage in health facilities?

options.A: Strict adherence to First-Expiry, First-Out rotation rules
options.B: Rough transport conditions crushing fragile cardboard packaging
options.C: Over-ordering supplies that subsequently exceed local demand
options.D: Improper storage exposing stock to high humidity and heat

explanation: FEFO is a best practice that prevents waste by ensuring older stock is used before it expires, unlike the other options which cause loss. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h7)
